newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Eight die, 14 hurt in Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Eight die, 14 hurt in Colombian violence.

text.p: At least eight people were killed, including a 6-year-old girl, and 14 others injured in political bloodletting across Colombia on Tuesday, authorities said.

In the northeast oil-production center of Barrancabermeja, National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels blew up a military truck, killing a 6-year-old girl playing nearby, regional army chief Maj. Juan Carlos Barrera told reporters. Three soldiers, one civilian and a 13-year-old girl were also injured in the blast.

In a separate attack, unidentified gunmen dragged three men active in Catholic Church social programs from their homes and shot them to death in the fishing village of Barranca Nueva in northern Bolivar province before dawn, Mayor Pedro Guerrero said.

It was not immediately known who was behind the violence although the region has witnessed a recent spate of attacks by right-wing death squads. Colleagues of the dead men, who asked not to be identified, believe the gunmen were searching for John Mahoney, a British priest who works in the community.

In a rural area near the town of Ituango in northwest Antioquia province, one soldier died and three soldiers and seven civilians were hurt when guerrillas dynamited an army truck, military sources said. They blamed the attack on the Cuban-inspired ELN, set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966.

In the fourth fatal incident, gunmen shot to death two former policemen and their driver in the southwest city of Cali. Police said the motives for the attack were unclear but two of the victims had been working as lawyers.
The attacks came just two days after the ELN shot down a helicopter in eastern Colombia, killing 20 soldiers and one civilian as they flew to repair an oil pipeline that had been blown up earlier.

In a statement late on Monday a combined right-wing paramilitary force, known as the United Self-Defense Groups of Colombia (AUC), said it was setting up a special commando to attack guerrillas that injured or killed children, the leading El Tiempo newspaper reported.

The move follows an attack by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest guerrilla force, on a farm in northwest Antioquia province last week in which 11-year-old twin brothers died.
